summary.text: Take \(n=7\). Since \(x\le y\le z\) and every permitted value of \(x\) is at least \(3\), one has \(x+y+z\ge 3x\ge 9\), contradicting \(x+y+z=7\); hence the strengthened representation claim fails independently of primality.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
a(n)=\#\bigl\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}^3:x\le y\le z,\ x+y+z=n,
\]
\[
2x-1,\ 2y-1,\ 2z-1,\ 2xy-1,\ 2xz-1,\ 2yz-1\text{ are all prime}\bigr\}.
\]
The conjecture consists of two assertions: first, that \(a(n)>0\) for every \(n>5\); and, moreover, that for every \(n>6\) there is such an ordered positive triple \(x\le y\le z\) in which
\[
x\in\{3,4,6,10,15\}.
\]
We disprove the combined conjecture by showing that its “moreover” assertion already fails for \(n=7\).

Suppose, for contradiction, that the conjecture is true. Since \(7>6\), its stronger clause supplies positive integers \(x,y,z\) satisfying
\[
x+y+z=7,\qquad x\le y\le z,
\]
with
\[
x\in\{3,4,6,10,15\},
\]
and with all six required numbers
\[
2x-1,\quad 2y-1,\quad 2z-1,\quad 2xy-1,\quad 2xz-1,\quad 2yz-1
\]
prime.

The primality conditions will not even be needed. From \(x\le y\le z\), we have \(y\ge x\) and \(z\ge x\). Consequently
\[
x+y+z\ge x+x+x=3x.
\]
Every member of \(\{3,4,6,10,15\}\) is at least \(3\), so this gives
\[
7=x+y+z\ge 3x\ge 9,
\]
which is impossible.

Equivalently, one can display the entire finite case split forced by the allowed set. If \(x=3\), then \(y,z\ge3\), so the sum is at least \(3+3+3=9\). If \(x=4\), the sum is at least \(12\). If \(x=6\), it is at least \(18\). If \(x=10\), it is at least \(30\). If \(x=15\), it is at least \(45\). None of these possibilities can have sum \(7\).

Thus there is no ordered positive triple summing to \(7\) whose least entry \(x\) belongs to \(\{3,4,6,10,15\}\), regardless of any primality requirements. Since \(7>6\), this is a counterexample to the “moreover” assertion. Therefore the conjunction asserted in the conjecture is false. This argument does not claim that the separate statement \(a(n)>0\) fails at \(n=7\); failure of the stronger universally quantified clause is by itself sufficient to disprove the stated combined conjecture.
